title: Moretta Fanese
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A warming layered coffee cocktail from Fano, combining rum, brandy, and anise liqueur with hot espresso and a float of lemon zest, historically enjoyed by local fishermen against the cold.
longDesc: Moretta was created for the fishermen of Fano, needing something both warming and energizing before heading out onto the cold Adriatic waters, and the drink's layered construction — spirits, sugar, coffee, and a twist of lemon — remains carefully preserved by local tradition.
steps: Combine the rum, brandy, and anise liqueur in a small pot and warm gently over low heat, without boiling.
Add the sugar to each glass.
Pour the warmed spirit mixture over the sugar in each glass.
Top with hot espresso, pouring gently to create a slight layered effect.
Garnish each glass with a twist of lemon peel.
chefTips: Warming the spirits gently before combining with the coffee helps meld the flavors and keeps the drink properly hot.
A twist of lemon peel is a traditional, essential garnish, adding a bright aromatic note.
This drink is traditionally enjoyed slowly, often after a meal on a cold day.
commonMistakes: Boiling the spirits, which can burn off too much of their flavor and alcohol.
Skipping the lemon peel garnish, which is a genuinely important part of the traditional presentation.
Using low-quality spirits, which affects the overall balance of this simple drink.
servedWith: Enjoyed on its own as a warming after-dinner drink
storage: Not applicable; made and consumed immediately.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed in moderation as an occasional warming treat.
culturalNote: Moretta Fanese originated among the fishermen of Fano on the Adriatic coast, historically enjoyed as a warming, energizing drink before heading out to sea in cold weather.
